items.text: Mohsen Rezaei said Donald Trump, influenced by Netanyahu, started a war against Iran which he called one of the biggest military mistakes in history. He added that the US naval fleet failed to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and Washington has turned to smuggling. These remarks came as the US continues its naval blockade of Iranian ports and Iran's oil exports have decreased.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported a drone attack on an oil tanker near Sohar port in Oman. Omani authorities are assisting in evacuating the crew, and damage assessment is not yet available. The IRGC Navy also reported an explosion and fire on a tanker due to hitting a naval mine.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, warned that the risk of a larger war in the Middle East has increased due to intensified fighting between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition. He highlighted the role of the Islamic Republic, the Revolutionary Guards, and the Houthis in this crisis. This situation could spread the fire of war from Yemen to the entire region.

Saudi Arabia has expanded its energy cooperation with Syria, Qatar, Kuwait, and Egypt. The Central Bank of Syria issued the first banking letter of credit to facilitate oil product transactions with Aramco. The Saudi energy minister signed three memorandums of understanding with Qatar, Kuwait, and Egypt.

Sepahan football team defeated Fajr Sepasi 6-1 in the eighth week of the Premier League. This was one of the highest-scoring matches of the league. With this victory, Sepahan reached 13 points and ranked fourth.

Reza Pahlavi condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and held the Islamic Republic responsible. He stated that if the Islamic Republic is overthrown, the region will achieve peace. He also mentioned that Saudi-Iran relations will be restored.

Mohammad Reza Bahonar stated in an interview that the provocation to continue the war is a Mossad conspiracy. He said the enemy uses intermediaries to incite Hezbollah forces towards war. These remarks were published on YouTube three days ago.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said commanders who threatened the US and Israel have been killed. He added that the fate of Mohsen Rezaei and other IRGC commanders could be similar. He also emphasized that the US and Israel still have intelligence and military superiority.

Tractor and Gol Gohar Sirjan football teams traveled to Najaf, Baghdad, and Muscat for their Asian matches. These journeys were difficult. In contrast, Esteghlal used a government VIP plane for their trip to Qatar.

The football teams Tractor and Gol Gohar first traveled to Iraq and then to Muscat for the Elite League and AFC Champions League matches. The Esteghlal team also traveled to Doha with an RJ aircraft belonging to the government protocol of the Islamic Republic. This report was presented by Raha Pourbakhsh in the Hat-trick program.

Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt condemned the attacks by Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia in a joint statement. They called for an immediate halt to these attacks and held the Houthis responsible for the consequences. The statement was issued following missile attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.

Amir Giti from Iran International said that the Islamic Republic's threats against US data centers and artificial intelligence could increase US security agencies' sensitivity towards Iranian students and specialists. He also pointed to tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi attacks, indicating the Islamic Republic's efforts to change regional dynamics. Giti added that the Islamic Republic has not been able to export its oil through the Strait of Hormuz.

Ghassan Ashour said that with the expansion of the Islamic Republic's confrontation from Israel to the United States, the importance of the Houthis for Tehran has increased. The Houthis can disrupt the oil and gas transit route from Bab al-Mandab. The Islamic Republic can use this threat to pressure global energy markets without accepting direct responsibility.

Gina Romero, the UN special rapporteur on freedom of peaceful assembly, announced she will join the 'No to Execution Tuesdays' hunger strike on Tuesday, October 13. She called for a halt to executions and independent monitoring of prisoners at risk of execution. Romero also highlighted political executions in Iran and human rights violations in protesters' cases.

Reuters reported that attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday left 13 dead and over 300 injured, leading to the airport's closure. The US Federal Aviation Administration on Sunday asked American airlines to exercise caution when flying to Saudi Arabia or transiting its airspace. The warning is valid until December 10.

Amir Hamidi, a national security expert, stated that the Islamic Republic's ability to disrupt shipping in the Strait of Hormuz with missiles, drones, or naval mines does not mean strategic control of this waterway. He added that Iran cannot impose its political will on the US by threatening to close or restrict passage in Hormuz. Hamidi warned that if threats against international shipping turn into action, the possibility of a defensive reaction and increased US pressure would be serious.

A group of Iranians living in Calgary protested in front of the city hall against executions in Iran and the verdicts in the Ali Khani Square case in Isfahan. They also commemorated the 88th birthday of Empress Farah Pahlavi and expressed support for the people inside Iran and Prince Reza Pahlavi. This report was published by Sepidar Valian from Iran International.

Ahmad Nadari said that the war is ahead and will not end soon. He added that the response to the revenge for the leader's blood has not been sufficient but they are moving in that direction. Nadari also stated that the reaction will be sufficient when full deterrence is achieved.

A ceremony was held in Beverly Hills to mark the 88th birthday of Empress Farah Pahlavi. Hundreds of Iranians attended the event. The ceremony highlighted her role and position in contemporary Iranian history.

Hossein Shariatmadari suggested using the passage of international fiber optic cables as leverage against the US and its allies. He emphasized Iran's right to block internet cables passing through the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. Shariatmadari criticized officials for neglecting this powerful leverage.

Zein al-Abedin Ghorbani Lahiji, former representative of the Supreme Leader in Gilan province and former Friday prayer leader of Rasht, passed away at the age of 93. He had served as head of revolutionary committees and courts in Gilan province. Ghorbani was a strong supporter of mandatory hijab.

Erfan Ghanei-Fard stated that despite government forces advancing around Taiz, a definitive shift in the balance of power in Yemen has not occurred. The Houthis still possess missile capabilities and the power to threaten Saudi Arabia. Stable control of Bab al-Mandab could increase pressure on the Houthis and reduce the Islamic Republic's ability to use this group to create regional insecurity.

Pegah Bani-Hashemi referred to May Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran, supporting Gina Romero's stance on executions. She said that the involvement of official UN figures in anti-execution campaigns can increase international attention to the situation of executions in Iran.

Anwar Gargash, the UAE foreign policy advisor, referred to attacks by the Islamic Republic and Houthis on Saudi Arabia. He stated that the security of the region's countries is interconnected. Targeting Saudi Arabia weakens the security of the UAE and Gulf countries.

Japan's Ministry of Defense announced that a Russian military reconnaissance aircraft violated Japan's claimed airspace on Friday, October 9. The aircraft flew over disputed islands between the two countries. Japanese fighters took off to intercept the Russian plane.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated at the university reopening ceremony that if he is martyred, better people will come to defend the country. He also said that selling gasoline at 1500 tomans is impossible and a sudden price increase would disrupt society. Pezeshkian emphasized that he would accept any correct guidance shown to him.

Fadahossein Maleki, a member of the National Security Commission, said the US cannot force neighboring countries to enforce sanctions against Iran. He described the US Treasury Secretary's statements as deflection and unfeasible. Maleki emphasized that popular ties prevent a complete blockade of Iran.

Dermot Gallagher stated that Tractor's goal against Esteghlal was correctly disallowed by VAR. Also, the goal by Sanat Naft against Persepolis was correctly allowed with no handball foul. These comments were made on the Hat Trick program.

Conflicting reports have emerged about the closure and reopening of the Enghelab and Keshvari sports complexes. The Ministry of Sports and the Sports Facilities Development Company have disagreements on this matter. Ultimately, the Enghelab sports complex resumed activities this morning.

A group of Iranians residing in the UK held the Mehregan festival in Birmingham on Sunday, October 11. During the event, the names of the immortal figures of the national revolution were recited. This news is based on a video received by Iran International.

Since August 6, the supplementary insurance for drivers, provided by Bimeh Dey, has been cut off due to government debt, and no one is responding. Teachers and students report economic difficulties and lack of facilities. Many businesses are closing due to inflation and reduced purchasing power.

Mohsen Rezaei warned about targeting artificial intelligence centers and data centers in the region. Ruhollah Rahimpour said the Islamic Republic can damage data centers in the Persian Gulf but cannot cause serious disruption to the global internet. These statements refer to security threats in the region.

Mohammadreza Zanouzi, owner of Tractor club, responded to Alireza Beiranvand's statements and behavior and explained the club's payments. He said players do not play just for money but with passion and loyalty. The club's CEO also criticized Beiranvand's behavior and stated that payments will continue as planned.

Abdulaziz bin Salman, Saudi Arabia's energy minister, said recent events have been serious and Saudi Arabia's response must be equally serious. He described the rapid repair of the East-West pipeline as a sign of preventive measures and emphasized the importance of energy security. These statements coincided with increased attacks by Yemeni Houthis on Saudi Arabia.
Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed Trump's proposal for a ceasefire on attacks on energy infrastructure. He said if Moscow stops these attacks, Kyiv will also stop similar attacks.

Masoud Pezeshkian stated that the cost of transporting each liter of gasoline is five thousand tomans, but it is sold at one thousand five hundred tomans. He compared economic issues to the process of treating a patient and said problems cannot be solved instantly. Changes must be made gradually.

A student in Yasuj says that IRGC forces stand armed daily near their school and threaten students to attend their gatherings and ceremonies. Those who do not attend are labeled as traitors. This issue was raised in a video sent to Iran International.

Kuwait's Foreign Ministry called the Houthi attacks on Saudi airports terrorist and condemned them. Kuwait demanded a firm stance from the international community to stop these attacks. It also stated that Saudi security is an integral part of Kuwait's and the Gulf Cooperation Council's security.

Shahin Rashidzadeh, a citizen from Baneh, was arrested by security forces on Saturday, October 4th. There is no information about his fate or whereabouts. This has increased the concerns of his family and relatives.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry, stated that message exchanges between Iran and the US continue through intermediaries and Tehran is reviewing Washington's latest proposal. He also rejected US claims about the Strait of Hormuz, saying the situation is a result of US and Israeli actions. Baqaei added that Iran is doing its part regarding the Strait of Hormuz and the US can continue its claims.

The sister of the late Javad Yousefi visited his grave and expressed her longing nine months after his death. Javad Yousefi, 33 years old, was killed on the evening of January 9, 2026, at Mikaeil Crossroad in Rasht. A video of this event was received by Iran International.

Masoud Pezeshkian warned about groundwater extraction in Tehran. He said this could lead to depletion of water reserves and drought. He compared the situation to the growth and death of microbes in a culture medium.

A video shows the grief of Nazanin Esmikani's family at her grave on International Day of the Girl. Nazanin Esmikani, a 17-year-old student, was killed on January 8, 2026, in Qazvin. The video was received by Iran International.

Abulfazl Shekarchi, senior spokesperson for Iran's armed forces, said the forces will not allow the enemy's regional order in West Asia to be renewed. He called US statements about control over the Strait of Hormuz propaganda and urged regional countries to leave the US security umbrella. Shekarchi warned that continued reliance on the US will have heavy costs.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, expressed concern about the war between Yemen and Saudi Arabia. He stated that Pakistan and Qatar remain mediators in negotiations with the US. He also described the issue of land transfer to Afghan nationals as a misunderstanding.

Manchester City fans waved inflatable bananas during the match against Liverpool at Anfield as a form of protest. This was City's first game after the independent commission's ruling on financial misconduct. The club denies the allegations and has appealed the decision.

Esmaeil Baghayi, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, responded to a question about the controversy surrounding his presence at the Arash orchestral event. He stated that his quick replies are directed at enemies, not his compatriots. This incident took place at the Espinas Hall in Tehran.

A student reported the presence of armed Revolutionary Guard forces at their school in Yasuj. The student said that students are threatened to attend the Guard's gatherings and ceremonies. Otherwise, they are labeled as traitors.

Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei stated they will not yield or surrender to arrogance. He also said corruption in the judiciary can undermine public trust in the judiciary and the system, and they are very sensitive to internal corruption. Ejei predicted they will witness the downfall of the US and Israel.

Alireza Beiranvand must be enlisted for military service on the first of Aban. His medical exemption requests were not approved. The location and manner of his service are not yet determined and will be announced in the coming days.

Masoud Pezeshkian spoke about the killing of students during the war. Morteza Kazemian responded, noting that the largest political massacre occurred during his government. He and other Islamic Republic officials did not mention the December massacre and lack the moral authority for such statements.

Yesterday, a minibus carrying seasonal workers collided with a car on the Piranshahr to Mirabad road. The accident resulted in injuries to five workers. No further details about the incident have been reported.

Andy Burnham, the UK Prime Minister, stated that the Islamic Republic is responsible for the attack on the Ferford base. The UK summoned the Iranian ambassador and imposed new sanctions on Tehran. The attack was definitely directed by the Revolutionary Guards.

The spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition announced that the country's air defense successfully intercepted and destroyed incoming missiles from Yemen. Minutes after an air threat warning, several explosions occurred in Riyadh, likely due to the interceptor missiles. The Saudi Civil Defense announced about 10 minutes later that the threat had been neutralized.

The interrogation session of 12 citizens related to the Qaleh Chenan case was held at the second interrogation branch of Karun County. Charges include moharebeh, baghi, disruption of public order, and conspiracy against national security. The accused are denied access to lawyers and meetings with their families.

At least six protests were held today, Monday, October 12, by retired telecommunications workers in Ahvaz, Kermanshah, Sanandaj, Isfahan, Khorramabad, and laid-off workers of Khavar spinning factory in Rasht. Their demands included unpaid wages and benefits, healthcare services, and job status clarification. These protests were reported in at least six locations.

The Israeli army announced the discovery and destruction of an underground tunnel network hundreds of meters long in southern Lebanon. Weapons such as Kalashnikovs, machine guns, and anti-tank missiles were found in these tunnels. The Israeli army stated it will not allow Hezbollah to harm Israeli civilians or soldiers.

Alireza Beiranvand attended the match between Nirooye Zamini Tehran and Karagostar after being dismissed from Tractor. The coach of Nirooye Zamini stated that Beiranvand's status with the team is still unclear. Tasnim News Agency reported that Beiranvand must begin his military service on November 1, 2026, and his medical requests were denied.

Esteghlal football team won 2-1 against Al-Gharafa Qatar in their second match of the Asian Elite League. Goals for Esteghlal were scored by Yaser Asani and Hossein Goodarzi. The victory was marked by Asani's superb goal and Habib Farabbasi's consecutive saves.

The match between Al-Nassr Saudi Arabia and Neftchi Uzbekistan in the Asian Champions League was delayed by one hour due to a security alert about a missile threat. Saudi authorities intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis towards Riyadh. After the security was confirmed, players returned to the field and the game continued.

Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have intensified. Saudi Arabia and the legitimate Yemeni government forces have launched heavy attacks on Houthi positions. Saudi Arabia has threatened a serious response, supported by Western allies including the UK.

Jaber Rajabi said that the mindset of part of the power in the Islamic Republic is based on an "all or nothing" logic and tries to ensure the regime's survival by holding regional security and economy hostage. He added that the Islamic Republic is expanding crises across the region to force others to make concessions. Rajabi also mentioned that regional countries might find short-term confrontation costs with the Islamic Republic less burdensome than enduring long-term threats.

The audio version 24 with Fardad Farahzad discusses the confrontation between Britain and the Islamic Republic. The involvement of the IRGC in a security plot has also been discovered. This topic was raised in the program.

Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh expressed happiness after Esteghlal's victory over Al-Gharafa in the Asian Elite League, emphasizing the team's effort and defense. He praised the players' performance and noted the challenges posed by bad weather and injuries to two players. Despite difficulties, he highlighted the team's unity and pride.

1,700 Iranian activists and families of victims supported awarding the 2026 Freedom Prize of the Friedrich Naumann Foundation to Reza Pahlavi. This support was announced in a letter prepared by the Patriotic Iranian Doctors group. The letter was delivered to the Friedrich Naumann Foundation.
